text:
ari: FYI customers reported failures when mounting object-store snapshots from last week. Restore jobs error: \`KMS: PermissionDenied\`. Saw RBAC sweep earlier today.
kevin: which snapshots? any tenant ids? paste minimal log.
ari: tenant=telluric-app, snap=ossnap-2026-03-22-03
```
2026-03-24T02:14:05Z ERROR restore_controller: decrypt key failed: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = caller does not have kms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
2026-03-24T02:14:05Z INFO restore_id=oss-restore-811
```
sre-bot: detected change: IAM policy update applied to serviceAccount:uploader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com at 2026-03-24T01:50:12Z
nina: That SA used to have kms.decrypt via a grant on keyrings/backups/keys/obj-store-key. RBAC cleanup removed a high-priv role and replaced with narrow storage roles.
ari: But uploader only uploads objects, it shouldn't need decrypt. Why was it decrypting during restore?
kevin: Historically uploader did client-side envelope encryption for multipart uploads to support partial re-encrypt. During restore pipeline we call a rewrap tool that used uploader identity to fetch DEKs and re-encrypt to new bucket. Looks like that path still runs in restores.
ops-tim: immediate fix options:
- re-add KMS grant to uploader SA (fast)
- change restore flow to execute under a dedicated decryptor SA that has KMS rights (safer)
- re-encrypt all existing snapshots with a different key (time-consuming)
nina: given customer impact, re-grant is quickest. But we should issue a scoped grant with a condition: only allow decrypt when request originates from our restore job service account or from the uploaders IP ranges.
ari: can Cloud KMS binding include condition by service account caller and resource name? we can add a condition requiring `request.time` or `resource.name`? Need to check.
kevin: Cloud KMS IAM supports conditional role bindings using expression language. We can add `request.auth.claims.email == 'uploader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com' && resource.name.startsWith('projects/.../cryptoKeys/obj-store-key')` but double-check syntax.
sre-bot: policy-diff shows current key binding only contains `backup-decryptor@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and `ops-kms@redwood.com` group.
ari: I've applied a temporary binding: `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` to `serviceAccount:uploader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with expiration in 30 minutes. Re-run of restore job passed for telluric-app.
kevin: good. Next steps:
- (SEC) map all places where uploader SA invokes KMS decrypt during any pipeline.
- (ENG) refactor restore pipeline to call a decryptor microservice running under `backup-decryptor` SA and remove uploader decrypt calls.
- (SRE) add an automated regression test: after any IAM/RBAC PR merge, run a quick restore smoke test for a small snapshot to catch missing key grants.
- (SEC) create an alert on KMS IAM policy changes for backups keyring (low noise filter: only alert on deletions/removals or role removals).
nina: I'll open ENGSEC ticket 2147 "restore path uses uploader SA for decrypt - remove direct KMS access" and link this thread + logs. Also will propose a conditional binding pattern for short-lived grants.
ops-tim: I'll draft an incident note for affected tenants and include mitigation + timeline. we should notify CS to reach out.
kevin: Also add a playbook item: before any RBAC pruning, run `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy --keyring=backups --format=json > baseline.json` and `diff` after changes; block PR if diff removes decrypt roles for any known pipeline SAs.
ari: one follow-up: we saw one snapshot still failing after the grant. It was created with an older DEK format. Nina, can you check if key versions matter?
nina: yes — old snapshots were encrypted using a legacy KEK version that is still active but its key rotation policy changed. We'll include a migration step in remediation plan.
ari: thanks. I'll revoke the temporary grant in 25 minutes and track progress. :thumbsup:
_note: Single-string messages field as required. No title.
